$comment: Known-open findings from rendered-resource-requests.ts, each with a reason and a lift
condition. An entry that matches nothing is STALE and fails the audit -- an acknowledgement
that outlives its defect is how a baseline becomes a lie.
Every liftsWhen here is the GATE ITSELF rather than a paraphrase of it. A lift condition
stricter than its gate keeps an entry alive after the defect is gone, which has cost this

entries.reason: 100m / 150Mi, AND IT IS REACHABLE NOW -- this is acknowledged because governing it is REFUSED, not because it cannot be expressed. The manifest-coordinate class added 2026-08-23 addresses cdi-operator.yaml document 7, containers[0] exactly, and this row WAS governed for one draft of that change before being backed out. `cdi-operator.yaml` is vendored byte-for-byte from upstream and `--resource-profile <rung> --apply` would rewrite it, making the checked-in copy diverge from what upstream ships. That invariant was stated in the catalogue before this work and is not mine to overturn as a side effect of a CPU budget. REACHING A FILE IS NOT A LICENCE TO EDIT IT.
entries.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN: `rendered-resource-requests.ts` stops reporting this exact key — which happens the moment EITHER a resourceClaim names the coordinate, OR the manifest stops declaring a request, OR the workload's replica count changes (the count is part of the key, so `replicas: 0` -> `1` makes this entry STALE and the new count OPEN, and the audit exits 1 on both). The condition IS the gate, not a paraphrase.

entries.reason: 5m / 16Mi on the `discover` container of the node-lan-hosts DaemonSet. It schedules today (a DaemonSet is one pod per node, counted x1), and it is acknowledged because governing it is INEXPRESSIBLE, not refused: a resourceClaim is keyed per rung on a replica count, and a DaemonSet has no replica count -- it is one pod per node by definition. This is node infrastructure (it bind-mounts /etc/hosts so the kubelet can resolve the LAN registry), not a rung-scaled workload, so there is no rung for a claim to name. 5m is the floor a kubectl poll loop needs.

entries.reason: 5m / 8Mi on the `apply` container of the node-lan-hosts DaemonSet -- the privileged sidecar that writes and bind-mounts the hosts block on the host. Same class as its `discover` sibling: one pod per node, no replica count, so no rung and no resourceClaim can express it. Acknowledged as node infrastructure, replica-count-keyed so scaling cannot happen silently (a DaemonSet cannot change replica count, which is exactly why the x1 key is stable here).

entries.reason: 5m / 8Mi on the `edge` container of the node-lan-hosts DaemonSet -- the HAProxy SNI router on the node's :443: it terminates TLS for the API hostnames (forwarding the REAL client address in X-Forwarded-For so the app's per-IP rate limit is per client, not one shared bucket) and passes every other hostname through to the Gateway. The home router can only port-forward to a device (the node), never to the Gateway's LB IP. Same class as its `discover` and `apply` siblings: one pod per node, no replica count, so no rung and no resourceClaim can express it. Acknowledged as node infrastructure; the x1 key is stable because a DaemonSet cannot change replica count.

entries.reason: 10m / 450Mi per pod across `replicas: 2` -- 20m / 900Mi in the totals. Same refusal as cdi and with a second artifact behind it: single-node-budget.json says of this exact file `NOT edited down to 1 on purpose: that manifest is vendored byte-for-byte so it stays 1:1 with what runs ... Editing it would make the checked-in copy diverge from the cluster it documents, which is a worse lie than this one.` A rung applier that rewrote it would do precisely what that sentence forbids. It is also the smallest of the reachable-but-refused set, so the budget argument for overriding the invariant is at its weakest here.

entries.reason: THE LARGEST LATENT REQUEST IN THE TREE: 4000m / 16384Mi, and it schedules nothing today because the Deployment ships `replicas: 0` and this Application's syncPolicy is manual-only. It is acknowledged rather than governed because IT CANNOT BE GOVERNED YET: a resourceClaim validates `pods >= 1`, so a row for a zero-replica workload would add a whole pod's reservation to every rung total and make the budget overstate by 4000m -- trading an under-count for an over-count. REPLICAS: 0 IS A REPRIEVE, NOT A FIT, exactly as gmod's gatekeeper webhook failure was; the key carries the replica count so the reprieve cannot expire silently.
